info.name: Zest — Zendesk ↔ Slack escalation service
info.description:
Every route the service exposes. Set the `baseUrl` variable (default http://localhost:8080).

The three /webhooks/zendesk/* requests sign themselves automatically when the collection variable `zendeskWebhookSecret` is non-empty; leave it blank for local dev, where the service skips verification.

request.description:
Liveness probe, registered outside the versioned base path so probes survive an API version bump.

200 → {"service":"zest","status":"ok"}

Ad-hoc Slack post. Both fields are required.

200 → {"message":"Message posted successfully"}
400 → validation error
502 → Slack rejected the call (e.g. invalid_auth, channel_not_found)

Adds tags to a ticket. `tags` must be a non-empty array of non-empty strings.

200 → {"message":"Tags updated successfully","tags":[...]}
400 → validation error
502 → Zendesk rejected the call

item.name: Zendesk webhooks

request.description:
Creates the Slack thread, then writes channel id + thread ts back onto the ticket's custom fields and adds the escalation tag.

Only `ticket_id` is required; every other field is optional and omitted from the Slack message when blank.

200 → {"message":"Escalation posted","ticket_id":"...","channel_id":"C...","thread_ts":"..."}

Note: a failure writing back to the ticket is reported as an error even though Slack already has the message, so Zendesk retries rather than leaving an orphaned thread.

Mirrors a ticket comment into the ticket's Slack thread. `ticket_id` and `comment` are required.

Optional `channel_id` / `ts` carry the join key directly; omit them and the service reads the custom fields off the ticket instead. Comments are truncated to 300 characters in the thread.

200 → {"message":"Posted to Slack thread","ticket_id":"...","skipped":false}
200 → {"message":"No Slack thread for ticket, update skipped",...,"skipped":true} when the ticket was never escalated

Mirrors a status transition into the thread. `ticket_id` and `status` are required.

Same thread-resolution and skip behaviour as the comment webhook.

Runs the same digest the scheduler posts, on demand. No request body.

Searches Zendesk for `type:ticket tags:<ESCALATION_TAG> updated<<cutoff>` where cutoff is now minus REPORT_STALE_AFTER, groups the results by status and posts one message as the report bot.

Posts an explicit all-clear when nothing is stale, so a broken schedule is distinguishable from a quiet week.

200 → {"message":"Report posted","tickets":3,"posted":true}
